newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Heavy hopes to join P&W engine project.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Heavy hopes to join P&W engine project.

text.p: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd said on Friday it would like to join a project at Pratt & Whitney, a unit of United Technologies Corp, to develop small aircraft engines.
A spokesman for Mitsubishi Heavy said, however, that it was not yet clear whether the U.S. company had made a final decision on proceeding with the development of the new engine, the PW6000.

Mitsubishi Heavy hopes to propose using the new engines, with a maximum thrust power of 24,000 pounds, in the the 90- to 100-seat YSX aircraft currently under development with Japanese government support.
But Mitsubishi Heavy faces competition from another engine development project led by Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries Co Ltd (IHI).
IHI has been jointly developing the CF34-8C engine with Kawasaki Heavy Industries Ltd and General Electric Co of the U.S.
A spokesman for IHI said the group would seek the use of its new engine, with maximum thrust power of 13,000 pounds, in the YSX programme.

Meanwhile, Mitsubishi Heavy is jointly developing the body of the new aircraft with four other Japanese manufacturers, including Kawasaki Heavy and Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd, as well as Boeing Co of the United States.

Separately from its work with Boeing and the four other Japanese firms, Mitsubishi Heavy is also conducting a feasibility study with Canadian aircraft manufacturer Bombardier Inc on the development of a 90- to 100-seat aircraft body, which could potentially be used by the YSX project, the Mitsubishi Heavy spokesman said. He added that the study is expected to be completed by the autumn of 1998.
